library_preparation_preflight.summary: micronaut-data-tx-jdbc provides DataSourceTransactionManager and related JDBC transaction support. It needs a real DataSource, which the artifact does not bring in. The sibling micronaut-data-jdbc 5.1.3 test project already uses Hikari and in-memory H2, and this library needs the same.

deterministic_setup.reason: Provides the Micronaut-managed DataSource that the JDBC transaction manager wraps. Same version as the sibling micronaut-data-jdbc 5.1.3 test project.
In-memory JDBC database, so no Docker is needed. Same version as the sibling micronaut-data-jdbc 5.1.3 test project.
Starts the Micronaut ApplicationContext for tests. Same version as the sibling micronaut-data-jdbc 5.1.3 test project.
Annotation processor for @Transactional and bean definitions. Same version as the sibling micronaut-data-jdbc 5.1.3 test project.

library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: I did not run any of this; it is based on reading the sibling project's build.gradle. Use the sibling tests/src/io.micronaut.data/micronaut-data-jdbc/5.1.3 project as the template, including its build.gradle, its user-code-filter.json and the graalvmNative agent conditional-mode block. Configure the datasource through ApplicationContext properties, for example `datasources.default.url=jdbc:h2:mem:testdb;DB_CLOSE_DELAY=-1`, `driverClassName=org.h2.Driver`, `username=sa` and `password=`. Then exercise the transaction manager through TransactionOperations, with `@Transactional` (jakarta.transaction or io.micronaut.transaction.annotation) on beans and with `executeWrite`/`executeRead`, covering commit and rollback. It may also need micronaut-data-processor as a testAnnotationProcessor, depending on the tests. If the tests need Micronaut Data repositories, add `io.micronaut.data:micronaut-data-processor:$libraryVersion` and micronaut-data-jdbc. micronaut-data-tx-jdbc is usually a transitive dependency of micronaut-data-jdbc, so check the resolved 5.1.3 classpath. If the tests use only tx-jdbc, keep the test scope to tx-jdbc APIs.
risks: Micronaut-generated bean definitions and annotation processing can make the native image need extra reflection or resource metadata.
The hikari and h2 versions are copied from the sibling project. They may not be the versions that resolve alongside tx-jdbc 5.1.3, so Gradle dependency resolution could conflict.
I did not check whether this artifact's own dependency set (micronaut-data-tx, micronaut-data-connection) already brings in some of these dependencies.
